actual_checks: Read the complete report, literal prompt, source notes and contribution metadata; checked reduced zero-framed n-dimensional normalization, formal-polynomial identities and the quantifiers in parts (a)–(c). Official metadata lists no prior contribution.

Independently checked the analytic identity argument: Delta(e^z)−1 cannot vanish on a neighborhood unless Delta=1; choose z away from 0 and 1 values, use the positive half-distance gap, and obtain every sufficiently large color. An unbounded subsequence has the same limit. No finite-color inference is made.

Checked HOMFLYPT specialization at a=1, unlink initialization and Conway uniqueness, then Delta(t)=Conway(t^(1/2)−t^(−1/2)). Alexander-trivial candidates and ordinary Jones detection remain outside scope.

scope_and_distinctness.exact_scope: Garoufalidis–Lê's analytic MMR theorem implies that for every knot with ΔK≠1, all sufficiently large normalized colours have Jn(K;q)≠1; even an unbounded subsequence of identically trivial colours forces ΔK=1. The HOMFLYPT identity likewise forces ΔK=1 by skein specialization. This does not decide ordinary Jones detection or rule out Alexander-trivial candidates.
